Oracle guard (Pyth) — required
Since Phase 3, this program can charge a fee that rises with a pool's price deviation from a Pyth oracle feed, up to the "Max fee" set below it — configure the oracle feed for each side above (or in the DLMM fields), or use the Localnet test fixtures shortcut while developing. This replaces the fixed-fee-only behavior of earlier versions of this program.
This program always settles fees in both tokens, based on trade direction — Single Side is a CLMM-only concept it doesn't implement.

Constant-product pools have no price range

Every constant-product pool covers the full price range by design — there's nothing to configure here. Your Step 3 deposit ratio sets the starting price, the same way real Raydium/Uniswap-style Standard AMM pools work.

Set the starting price & bin range

Bins above the active bin receive Amount A only; bins below receive Amount B only; the active bin receives both — this split is applied for you automatically.

Constant-Product AMM

Classic x·y=k pools — advanced/manual panels for managing liquidity here, one raw on-chain call at a time. Looking to swap? Head to Swap. Looking to create a pool? Head to Liquidity — the guided Create wizard now lives there.
Picking a pool here fills in Mint A / Mint B everywhere on this tab — no need to type or paste any address.

DLMM — Concentrated Liquidity

Meteora-style bin-based pools — a separate set of pools, mints and positions from the constant-product AMM (see the AMM tab). Advanced/manual panels only — looking to swap? Head to Swap. Looking to create a pool? Head to Liquidity.
Picking a pool here fills in Mint A / Mint B everywhere on this tab — no need to type or paste any address.

0. Quick Setup

Automates the manual steps below. Each button still needs a wallet approval per transaction, but you no longer have to copy/paste mint addresses between panels — they fill in automatically everywhere.
Quick Setup uses the active pair above if one exists, otherwise it creates a fresh one — then initializes the pool, deposits starter liquidity, and loads the pool info automatically.

1. Create Test Mint (helper)

Creates a new test SPL token (6 decimals) and mints 1,000,000 units into your wallet — use this instead of finding a real token to test with.

Governance Status

GlobalConfig is a single, program-wide account — every pool this program governs shares it. Pool creation fails until it's initialized and both mints are allowlisted below.

2. Governance Setup & Actions

One-time setup (Initialize Global Config) plus the governance-only actions used while testing: allowlisting a mint before its first pool, pausing new pool creation, and independently verifying a Squads multisig against governance_authority.
Initialize Global Config (once per deployment)
In production this should be a Squads vault PDA (see Verify Squads Multisig below) — for local/devnet testing, leaving both blank uses your connected wallet as governance_authority and a fixed test keypair as emergency_authority, matching this program's own test suite convention.
Allowlist a mint (required before its first pool)
Pause / unpause new pool creation
Verify Squads multisig (permissionless, anyone can check)
Reads the REAL Squads v4 account on chain and confirms it owns governance_authority's vault — this program never re-implements Squads' own approval logic, so this is how you independently check governance_authority really is backed by the multisig it claims to be (see governance.rs's module doc comment).

Manual / Advanced Panels

The same actions as the guided panels above, broken into individual raw on-chain calls — useful for testing edge cases or when you already know a pool's addresses.
